questions.question: What does a Suspense boundary do?
options: Catches errors thrown by its children
Shows a fallback while something in its subtree is not ready
Delays rendering by a fixed time
Retries failed network requests
questions.explanation: Suspense declares a loading fallback for a subtree. Catching errors is the job of an error boundary.

questions.question: Why does a plain fetch inside useEffect not trigger Suspense?
options: Effects run too late
Suspense requires something to suspend, and a plain fetch does not integrate with that mechanism
fetch is not supported in React
The component must be lazy
questions.explanation: Suspense is a protocol. Lazy components and Suspense-enabled data layers participate in it; a manual fetch in an effect does not, so you handle loading state yourself.

questions.question: What is wrong with calling lazy inside a component body?
options: lazy cannot be called in a function
A new component type is created on every render, so the subtree remounts and refetches
The import runs twice
It only works with named exports
questions.explanation: Declare lazy components at module level. A fresh type each render means React unmounts and remounts the whole subtree.

questions.question: What does a module loaded with lazy need?
options: A named export matching the component
A default export
A .lazy.js file extension
To be registered in the router
questions.explanation: `lazy` expects the resolved module to have a `default` export. For a named export, map it in the then callback.

questions.question: What does startTransition do to a state update?
options: Delays it by a fixed number of milliseconds
Marks it as non-urgent so React can interrupt it to handle urgent updates first
Runs it in a web worker
Batches it with other updates
questions.explanation: It changes priority. Urgent updates such as typing are handled first, and an in-progress transition can be abandoned and restarted.

questions.question: When would you use useDeferredValue instead of useTransition?
options: When the update is urgent
When you receive a value but do not control the state update that produced it
When the component is lazy loaded
When you need a loading spinner
questions.explanation: `useTransition` needs access to the setter. `useDeferredValue` works with a value you were handed, for example a prop.

questions.question: What happens when an update inside startTransition causes a component to suspend?
options: The Suspense fallback replaces the content immediately
React keeps showing the current content until the new one is ready
The transition is cancelled
An error is thrown
questions.explanation: Transitions avoid hiding good content. React holds the existing screen rather than flashing a fallback, which is what makes navigations feel smooth.

questions.question: Which action is a poor candidate for an optimistic update?
options: Liking a post
Toggling a checkbox
Processing a payment
Adding a comment
questions.explanation: Optimism suits actions that almost always succeed and are easy to undo. Showing a payment as complete before it is confirmed misleads the user.
